- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to avoid undershoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 3–5 days to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and model forecast is below recent 10-day average, model underestimates upward momentum; increase forecast by 1–3% to match sentiment-driven bias.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.27–0.80), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days to match sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates near-term volatility; cap forecast deviation from 14-day moving average at ±3% to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00–0.27) and price is trending down, model tends to underestimate further decline; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast.
